clue.text: Bear away the flag

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, tolerate it
read as two words, 'a way': A plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry off the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' must be split into 'a way', giving A and RD (road); the clue's surface sense of carrying something off is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or ensign, especially one carried in battle or on parade.

clue.text: Sort of plug for a top boxer?

definitions.text: Sort of plug for a top boxer?

parts.words: Sort of plug for a top boxer?
parts.note: a kind of plug in a car engine, which split into two words describes the monarch of sparring

explanation.walkthrough: Split as SPAR KING it is a champion sparrer; whole, it is the ignition plug in a petrol engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ignition plug in a petrol engine fires the fuel; the split form suggests a champion pugilist.

clue.text: Sanctioning copying out of a book

indicators.note: out of means the copying word lies outside the book, wrapped around it

parts.note: aping is copying
Prov is the abbreviation for Proverbs, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Approval is given to plagiarising a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of a book' reads as copying from a text, but 'out of' is the container signal: the copying word sits outside the book abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Approving means giving official consent or endorsement.

clue.text: Illegitimate Claud is of aristocratic stock

indicators.note: illegitimate suggests something not properly ordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Claud, born out of wedlock, has noble blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means of or belonging to a duke, the highest rank of the peerage.

clue.text: Instrument has a note missing so send for another

indicators.note: missing means the note is lost from the instrument's name

parts.note: a recorder is a woodwind instrument
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is short of a note, so a replacement must be ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to order again, requesting a fresh supply.

clue.text: Black tar round a rock

indicators.note: the black-and-tar pair goes round the little word a, holding it inside

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
a tar and a salt are both slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Dark pitch has been smeared around a boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like the black sticky stuff but is a sailor, i.e. SALT. B and SALT go round A: B-A-SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, the commonest type of solidified lava.

clue.text: Can be transferred by foreign sailor to' the French

parts.note: alien means foreign
AB is an able seaman
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Something may be passed on by an overseas seaman to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienable property is property whose ownership may legally be handed over to another.

clue.text: Bother! The, public address system won't start

indicators.note: won't start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name used for any public address system

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry as the loudspeakers fail to come on.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannoy is a trademark that in Britain means any public-address loudspeaker system; 'won't start' drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an imperative: to bother someone is to irritate or pester them.

clue.text: French is doubled up with fever caused by this' fly

definitions.text: with fever caused by this' fly

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
doubled means the French word appears twice in a row

parts.note: est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A French patient doubled over with fever from an insect bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled up' looks like one phrase for being bent in pain; 'doubled' gives ESTEST and 'up' turns it to TSETSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The African tsetse insect carries the parasite causing sleeping sickness, a feverish disease.

clue.text: Not so' long: ago soldiers had little money

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cent is a small coin, one hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: Only recently the troops were short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent happened a short time back.

clue.text: Lavender jelly

definitions.meaning: an old name for spike lavender, a Mediterranean species
a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a species of lavender plant and a clear savoury gelatine used for glazing cold food.

clue.text: "Keep ye the law — be swift in all ______" (Kipling)

definitions.text: "Keep ye the law — be swift in all ______" (Kipling)

parts.words: "Keep ye the law — be swift in all ______" (Kipling)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing last word of this line from Kipling's verse The Law of the Jungle

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the printed clue ends with a blank after 'all', lost in the copy. The line from Kipling's The Law of the Jungle ends 'be swift in all obedience'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line urges prompt compliance with the law, which is the virtue the missing word names.

clue.text: Ken cooked, Ken glowed

indicators.note: cooked here means the following letters are doctored, rearranged like cooked books

explanation.surface: Ken did the cooking and Ken was flushed from the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Ken' is not a man's name but the noun meaning range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is a Scots word for understanding or the range of what one knows, so it equals learning or awareness.

clue.text: An uncertain poet

definitions.meaning: Alfred ..., English poet, author of The Highwayman

explanation.definitionFit: A waverer's 'no... yes' run together gives the surname of Alfred Noyes, the English poet famous for The Highwayman.

clue.text: Therein possibly lies the opposite of both

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of therein could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A riddle claims that inside something lies the reverse of 'both'.
explanation.definitionFit: Where 'both' includes each of two, the contrasting word excludes each of two: not one and not the other.

clue.text: Passes fish — sign that a deal has been agreed

definitions.text: sign that a deal has been agreed

parts.note: hands means passes, as in 'hands it over'
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone passes over a fish, sealing a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking palms is the customary gesture sealing a bargain.

clue.text: Army rejects dull brown jacket

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: rejects suggests throwing back, so the word for dull brown is read backwards

parts.note: drab is a dull light brown colour

explanation.surface: The military turns down a dreary khaki coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' reads as the army turning something down, but it is the reversal signal acting on the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic or jerkin, as worn by heralds or knights over armour.

clue.text: Crack rate problem by gambling here?

indicators.note: problem signals that the letters pose a puzzle to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Solving a betting-odds puzzle, one place to bet comes to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like 'solve', but CRACK and RATE are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters bet on horses or dogs at the course where races are run.

clue.text: Councillor supported by journalist who needs paying

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: an editor is a journalist

explanation.surface: A local politician is backed by a newspaperman who is owed money.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is someone to whom money is owed.

clue.text: An American lawyer includes information in the programme

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A US attorney adds some facts to the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information ('get the gen').
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be dealt with at a meeting: its schedule or plan.

clue.text: Specify when writing on the wall.

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
the writing on the wall is a sign of things to come, after the warning in the Book of Daniel

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to say when graffiti appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to allot or designate, naming something specifically.

clue.text: One making a hole for a sleeper?

definitions.text: One making a hole for a sleeper?

parts.words: One making a hole for a sleeper?
parts.note: a sleeper is also a small ring or stud worn in a newly pierced ear to keep the hole open, so the person punching ears is meant, not someone digging a bed

explanation.walkthrough: A 'sleeper' suggests a railway sleeper or someone asleep, but it is the small earring that keeps a fresh piercing open.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who punches holes for ear studs is a body-jewellery technician by trade.

clue.text: Kneecap Irishman seen with a girl

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish man's name
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Irish fellow is spotted with his girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the anatomical name for the bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Bleat about Grandma's fruit

indicators.note: about means the bleat goes around the grandmother word

parts.note: baa is a sheep's bleat
nan is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone complains about Granny's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with yellow skin.

clue.text: Fool around near the gorge

indicators.note: around tells us the word for fool sits either side of the word for near

parts.note: an ass is a fool
by means near, as in 'stand by the door'

explanation.surface: Some idiot is messing about close to the ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm, much like a gorge or ravine.

clue.text: Kirk's in the rising river — this vessel may save him

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation inside the river's letters
rising in a down clue means the river's name reads upwards

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
kirk is Scots for church, abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk is drowning in a swelling river and a boat may rescue him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kirk' suggests Star Trek's captain, but it is Scots for church (CH); the Tay reversed gives YAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor boat, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Cronus almost consumed a lot of dripping

indicators.note: almost means the god's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Cronus is the Greek god identified with the Roman Saturn
consumed means ate
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a lot

explanation.surface: The Titan who swallowed his children nearly devoured a good deal of fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SATURN to SATUR; dripping looks like cooking fat (a British staple), but it means soaking wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturated means soaked through, so wet that water runs off.

clue.text: State actual figure

parts.note: real means actual
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone states a true number.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or country.

clue.text: Port for Michael, say

definitions.meaning: the Russian White Sea port, usually written Arkhangelsk
Michael is one of the chief angels in scripture, an example of the rank

explanation.definitionFit: The Russian seaport takes its name from the chief angel Michael, who is himself an example of that high heavenly rank.

clue.text: Expect to be a singer

parts.note: a wait is one of a band of carol singers going from door to door at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to become a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: WAITS were street carol singers in Britain at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to look forward to it or wait for it.

clue.text: The man breaks into a song

indicators.note: breaks into suggests the two words are smashed into pieces and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A fellow suddenly starts singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks into a song' reads as bursting into song, but 'breaks' is the anagram signal on THE MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a solemn song, such as a national hymn or church choral piece.

clue.text: Farmer's punch

definitions.meaning: a farm hand who cuts and dries grass for fodder; the 's stands for 'is'
a wild swinging blow in boxing

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a farm worker making hay and a heavy swinging punch in boxing.
